Marp CLI does not bundle a browser. Converting a deck to PDF, PPTX or images requires an installed Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Mozilla Firefox. The standalone binaries bundle Node.js, not a browser.

claims.claim: Marpit's global directives are exactly headingDivider, lang, style and theme. There is no `dir` directive; an unrecognised front-matter key is silently ignored, so `dir: rtl` has no effect and produces no error.
Marpit requires an `@theme` metadata comment in a theme CSS file for the theme to be referenced by name from a deck's front matter.

Marp has no engine-level RTL support. RTL is achieved entirely through CSS in a custom theme: `direction: rtl` and `text-align: right` on `section`. There is no front-matter directive that does it; Marpit's global directives are only headingDivider, lang, style and theme. Confirmed against Marp CLI 4.5.0 (2026-07-17).

claims.claim: python-pptx 1.0.2 (requires_python >=3.8) is the current release on PyPI. It exposes no paragraph RTL property, so the OOXML rtl attribute must be set through the XML layer.
claims.raw_snippet: Create, read, and update PowerPoint 2007+ (.pptx) files.

claims.claim: Per OOXML (ISO/IEC 29500) DrawingML, right-to-left is the boolean `rtl` ATTRIBUTE on the paragraph-properties elements `<a:pPr>` (CT_TextParagraphProperties) and `<a:lvl1pPr>`..`<a:lvl9pPr>` -- e.g. `<a:pPr algn="r" rtl="1">` -- which is exactly what PowerPoint writes and what LibreOffice and Google Slides import honor. DrawingML has NO `<a:rtl>` element anywhere (datypic e-a_rtl-1.html is 404) and run properties `<a:rPr>` / `<a:defRPr>` (CT_TextCharacterProperties) carry no `rtl` attribute, so there is no run-level direction toggle (unlike WordprocessingML's `<w:rtl/>`). Inline LTR runs inside an RTL paragraph render LTR via the Unicode bidi algorithm; ambiguous boundaries are fixed with bidi controls (LRM U+200E, LRI U+2066 / PDI U+2069) in the text, not XML.

claims.claim: python-pptx exposes no font-embedding API. The OOXML flag is embedTrueTypeFonts on the <p:presentation> root element, reachable as prs._element; there is no Presentation.presentation attribute, and <p:presentationPr> is the root of a separate part rather than a child of <p:presentation>.
claims.verified_via: executed against an installed python-pptx 1.0.2: prs._element.set('embedTrueTypeFonts','1') round-trips into ppt/presentation.xml, while prs.presentation raises AttributeError

claims.claim: The Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm operates on a paragraph's character stream. Rule P1 splits text into paragraphs and rule P2 finds the first character of type L, AL or R. A DrawingML run boundary is not an input to the algorithm, so splitting or merging runs cannot change reordering. LRM and LRM-class marks are strong characters whose ordering effect equals a strong directional character; isolation requires LRI/PDI.
claims.raw_snippet: In each paragraph, find the first character of type L, AL, or R while skipping over any characters between an isolate initiator and its matching PDI

claims.claim: The Google Slides API sets paragraph direction via ParagraphStyle.direction, with enum values LEFT_TO_RIGHT and RIGHT_TO_LEFT, applied through UpdateParagraphStyleRequest in batchUpdate. Direction is not inherited and defaults to LEFT_TO_RIGHT when unset.
claims.raw_snippet: If unset, the value defaults to LEFT_TO_RIGHT since text direction is not inherited.
